alex_devex: Heads up — ran into a puzzler yesterday: Redwood JS SDK works in next dev but throws in Vercel Edge middleware during prod deploy. stack: TypeError: crypto.getRandomValues is not a function.

sam_runtime: ah yeah, Web Crypto surface varies on edge. where are we calling getRandomValues? module init?

alex_devex: in auth nonce generation inside the client - it executes at import time. local dev uses node poly so silent. on Vercel Edge their runtime wrapper doesn't expose getRandomValues the same way. also saw `ReferenceError: require is not defined` in another report when customers bundled using commonjs.

li_ts: typing/exports note: our package.json points main -> cjs and module -> esm, but we don't ship a clear edge-specific entry. TS users import types from default and sometimes get the cjs d.ts. If we add a subpath like "redwood/edge" we can ship edge.d.ts.

maria_prodeng: two practical options: (1) make the default ESM import edge-safe (maybe simplest), or (2) add a documented subpath `redwood/edge` that is explicitly edge-only so middleware authors import that. the subpath avoids breaking existing require users.

sam_runtime: implementation idea: build a separate edge ESM bundle (no node:* imports), target browser platform in bundler, and lazy-evaluate crypto helper (use globalThis.crypto?.getRandomValues in runtime wrapper). avoid calling at module top-level.

alex_devex: I prototyped dist/edge.mjs and a subpath export: "./edge": { "import": "./dist/edge.mjs", "types": "./dist/edge.d.ts" }. Vercel resolver didn't auto-pick a custom condition so consumers must explicitly import from 'redwood/edge'.

li_ts: adding dist/edge.d.ts and export map subpath is the safest for TS resolution. also add a tiny TS test that `import type {Client} from 'redwood/edge'` resolves. avoids relying on conditional exports that differ across bundlers.

maria_prodeng: docs change: update Next.js middleware quickstart to show `import { createClient } from 'redwood/edge' // for middleware` and add a troubleshooting snippet explaining crypto/require errors and the reason. also add a short migration note for users who were `require('redwood')` in middleware (they should switch to subpath or runtime-safe default).

sam_runtime: tests: smoke with vercel dev + esbuild bundle test importing edge subpath. add CI step that does a minimal middleware bundle using the edge entry.

alex_devex: plan: PR will (1) add edge ESM build (browser target), (2) add "./edge" export subpath with types, (3) guard crypto usage behind runtime-detect, (4) update quickstart and templates to use edge import. aiming for patch release this week.

vercel-bot: deploy preview created for PR 637: https://deploy-preview.example.com — includes sample middleware page using `redwood/edge`.

li_ts: small note: also watch out for `globalThis.crypto.subtle` vs `getRandomValues` surface — some runtimes only expose subtle. implement a minimal shim: prefer getRandomValues, else derive random using subtle.digest on a counter as fallback (documented).

maria_prodeng: good. Also add a linter rule in our Next example repo to prefer `redwood/edge` in middleware files so new users copy the right import.

alex_devex: thanks team. PR link will be posted once ready. will ping customers who reported it to try the preview. :thumbsup:
